newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas boosted by western heat, futures.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas boosted by western heat, futures.

text.p: U.S. spot natural gas prices moved higher Monday due to a sharp rise in cooling demand in the West and a rally in the futures market, sources said.
On the Louisiana Gulf Coast, swing prices at the Henry Hub were quoted up an average of one to three cents to $2.21 early and as high as $2.30 shortly before nomination deadlines.
Pulling the cash market higher was the rise of September gas futures to a high of $2.34, up 10.1 cents on the day.
In the Midwest, swing prices gained about one cent to $2.15-2.16, with Chicago city-gate gas quoted up at $2.31-2.36.

In the Permian Basin market, prices jumped an average of seven cents to about $2.15-2.16 as temperature highs in parts of northern California topped 100 degrees F. Similar weather was evident in the Southwest, according to Weather Services Corp.
San Juan basin gas was also pumped up about 10 cents to $2.10-2.14, while southern California border prices soared to about $2.27-2.35.
In the East, New York city gate gas held in the low-to-mid $2.40s, traders said, as temperatures dropped to about five to 10 degrees F below normal in the area.
